mln-rs's picture sits within 0.002% and 0.12 px of the one GL JS's camera formulas give in f64; GL JS's images are 0.05% smaller than that and 0.2 to 0.3 px higher, and its soft-edged and crisp images differ from each other by 0.12 px, so which one a device comes near depends on how it filters the drapes. The rows where a checker's edge crosses a pixel's center then differ: 240 of 65,536 px on RADV, 1,663 on Mesa 26.0.8's lavapipe and 1,899 on Apple's paravirtual device. It can run again when the globe's picture and GL JS's agree to under 0.1 px
